about: WiFi chips irate-box knows: how to recognise each (USB IDs, the ID it shows in USB storage mode, its driver, or drivers for a family), what it can do, where its driver comes from when the kernel has none, and test results, ours and others'. Read by hub/knownradios.py. A row with no usb_ids is matched by its driver alone. Results from other projects are credited to them.

notes: Starts as a USB drive (a69c:5721): an eject switches it to WiFi.
Its driver's ID table lacks 368b:8d81: it works told to treat it as a69c:8d81 (new_id).
A reset of the whole USB device sends it back to storage mode; a reset of its WiFi interface comes back in about 4 s.
Its driver cannot move the radio into another network namespace.
Keeps its own regulatory country (self-managed): the box's WiFi country setting does not apply to it.

tested.result: Works. Client: 2.3 ms to the router with power saving off, 8.2 ms on. Hotspot: 1–8 ms idle, 109–118 ms under load; 20-minute soak with no loss. Hotspot beside a client link: on the link's channel, the link unaffected. Once, the box hung when it started as a hotspot under load (not reproduced).

notes: Built into the Luckfox Lyra Zero W.
Its firmware can go silent for more than 4 s: the driver then marks its command queue dead until reloaded, and a USB reset does not always bring the chip back (a power cycle does).

Its hotspot follows the link's channel. With the hotspot on a channel of its own, the firmware can stop while the link joins or roams: 16 stalls in 2026-10-22's tests, all with the two on different channels, none in 161 joins on the same one.

tested.result: Identified only (its WiFi is the board's only link). Long-running use since 2026-10-09: firmware stalls under roaming and access points that vanish.

notes: Cannot turn power saving on.
Uses one channel at a time: a hotspot beside a client link must be put on the link's channel.
A second interface needs its own MAC address.

tested.on: Raspberry Pi 3B+, kernel 6.18.50+rpt-rpi-v8 (sold as "VIA USB2.0 WLAN", 040d:3801)
tested.result: The steadiest 2.4 GHz hotspot: a flat 20-minute soak at 36–38 Mbit/s, no loss. Under load 72–94 ms average. Back from a driver reset in 4.1 s.

source.name: an out-of-tree rtl8188eus driver, for hotspot mode (candidate: aircrack-ng's)

notes: The kernel's rtl8xxxu has no hotspot mode for it (6.18); older kernels' staging r8188eu had one.
Cannot turn power saving on, and reports no signal strength.
Sometimes fails to join a hotspot within 40 s.

tested.result: Client only. Joins the router in 6.6 s, 6.4 ms average. Back from a driver reset in 2–4 s. Twice didn't associate with another radio's hotspot.
Recommended: 0.25 W idle, 0.4 W transmitting (TP-Link TL-WN725N v2, TL-WN722N v4, Edimax EW-7811Un v2).

notes: Power saving hurts it as a hotspot: 65–73 ms (up to 490 ms idle) with it on, about 5 ms off.
Moves its hotspot onto the client link's channel by itself; the link's latency rises to about 30 ms while both run.

tested.result: Hotspot under load 31–81 ms average; a 20-minute soak with no loss (two throughput dips).

notes: Among the best-supported dual-band dongles (mt76x0u for the MT7610U).
WiFi 6.
Very common, cheap.
Very common, cheap; client only.
In the kernel's rtw88 from about 6.2; older kernels need an out-of-tree driver.

source.name: an out-of-tree driver for kernels without rtw88's support (candidates: morrownr's or aircrack-ng's)

notes: Very common dual-band dongles, only recently in the kernel.

tested.result: RTL8821AU not working (TP-Link Archer T2U Plus).
